### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1; managed app-server 0.162.1.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6.1-Sol was selected, but reproduction requires no model request.

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu Linux, x86_64.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Initially noticed in Herdr 0.8.2. Independently reproduced using the native standalone Codex binary in a separate PTY, with HERDR_* caller context removed and no shell wrapper.

### Codex doctor report

Native diagnostics confirmed CLI and managed server both use 0.162.1, the daemon is running, config parses, and state databases pass integrity checks. Full report omitted because it contains unrelated local workspace metadata.

### What issue are you seeing?

Connecting to the same machine's managed daemon using `codex --remote unix://` silently changes the new session's working directory from the terminal's project directory to the daemon's directory (home in this reproduction).

This affected a workflow where terminal and phone attach to the same app-server. The client process had the correct launch cwd, but the resulting session used home. Explicit `--cd` fixes it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have the managed daemon running from a different directory, for example home (`codex remote-control start`). Do not stop or restart a daemon serving active work just to reproduce this.
2. Create an empty synthetic directory and launch the native binary directly:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/codex-cwd-repro/project
cd /tmp/codex-cwd-repro/project
command codex --remote unix:// --no-alt-screen
```

3. Run the local `/status` command. Observed: `Directory: ~` and the existing managed Unix control socket as `Server`. No task prompt was submitted.
4. Exit that empty TUI and run the control:

```bash
command codex --remote unix:// --cd "$PWD" --no-alt-screen
```

Observed: the new session shows `/tmp/codex-cwd-repro/project` as its directory.

### What is the expected behavior?

For the canonical same-host managed daemon endpoint, preserve the terminal's launch directory, or make the requirement for explicit `--cd` clearly visible before a new task starts in a different directory.

I understand that a genuinely remote workspace may intentionally default to the server directory. This report concerns the surprising same-host managed-daemon case; it is not a request to blindly forward local paths to every WebSocket or forwarded Unix endpoint.

### Additional information

Source inspection at commit `78dc2503840d05f4411ae184bb5560ef327fce3c` suggests why:

- [`AppServerTarget::uses_remote_workspace`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/78dc2503840d05f4411ae184bb5560ef327fce3c/codex-rs/tui/src/lib.rs#L342) returns true for `Remote` regardless of the Unix transport.
- [`config_cwd_for_app_server_target`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/78dc2503840d05f4411ae184bb5560ef327fce3c/codex-rs/tui/src/lib.rs#L919) returns no local cwd for that target.
- The nearby `config_cwd_for_app_server_target_omits_cwd_for_remote_sessions` test explicitly covers a Unix socket. This may therefore be intentional remote semantics with a missing distinction or diagnostic for the canonical local-daemon attachment, rather than a simple cwd propagation omission.

A possible direction is to retain local-daemon semantics when explicitly attaching to the canonical same-host control endpoint, or warn/document that `--remote unix://` requires `--cd` to retain launch cwd. Preserve truly remote filesystem semantics and explicit `--cd` choices.

Related but different: #31317 concerns the resume picker's cwd filter despite explicit `--cd`; #42457 concerns hook cwd; #46145 concerns workspace roots despite a correct explicit cwd. Here, the new session's directory itself changes when `--cd` is omitted.

Local workaround: pass `--cd "$PWD"` when launching the interactive client against the shared local server. No private project names, conversation content, account identifiers, or real session IDs are included here.

1. The Store installed stable build `26.1007.9446.0` around 14:24. The older desktop run's last log entry was at 17:58:58.

3. A fresh user-data directory launched under an elevated token still showed zero visible windows over 60 seconds. An AUMID launch likewise showed zero windows over 45 seconds.
4. At 18:56–19:01 the stable package was uninstalled and reinstalled from Microsoft Store. Its first launch with no restored profile produced five processes, zero windows, and no new desktop log directory. Restoring the saved profile did not change the result.

- No new stable desktop log, CrashDump, or WER crash report was available for the no-window reproduction.

## Expected behavior

The stable desktop package should create a visible window or surface a usable startup error. Please investigate the stable 26.1007.9446.0 startup/renderer path and advise on a supported workaround. The Beta build works on this machine, but stable remains installed and starts headlessly.

I searched open and closed Mermaid issues and PRs before filing this focused follow-up. I found that comment but no dedicated open issue for node-label line breaks, and no open Mermaid PR. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Start Codex CLI 0.162.1 in Ghostty with Mermaid rendering enabled. 2. Ask Codex to reply with a fenced `mermaid` block containing exactly this source: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Codex reply
completed"] --> B["Rendered in Ghostty"] ``` 3. Wait for the assistant to finish the reply. 4. Observe the unsupported-features notice and raw Mermaid source instead of a diagram. A smaller equivalent case for a regression test is: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["one
two"] --> B["done"] ``` A useful control replaces only `
` with a space: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["one two"] --> B["done"] ``` The two-node `Codex reply` case was observed in the actual CLI. The smaller case and control above follow from source inspection and were not separately executed in a Rust test during this investigation. ### What is the expected behavior? Render a terminal-native diagram with `Codex reply` and `completed` on separate lines inside the same node. Preserve the exact Mermaid source for raw display, copy, and session history. Supporting common line-break forms such as `
`, `
`, and `
` would address the observed use case without accepting arbitrary HTML. Multiline label width should reflect the displayed lines. Existing resource limits and a fallback for a diagram that genuinely cannot fit can remain. ### Additional information **Root cause and unreleased-code check** At immutable `main` commit [`cd8d61b223d95fd540bb646d627e7f0e7cfa6146`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/cd8d61b223d95fd540bb646d627e7f0e7cfa6146): - [`check_label`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/cd8d61b223d95fd540bb646d627e7f0e7cfa6146/codex-rs/mermaid/src/parse.rs#L173-L187) rejects markup whenever `<` is followed by an ASCII letter. All three `
` forms therefore return `RenderError::Unsupported` before layout. - [The TUI adapter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/cd8d61b223d95fd540bb646d627e7f0e7cfa6146/codex-rs/tui/src/markdown_render/mermaid.rs#L39-L60) maps that result to the notice above and retains the source. - The entire `codex-rs/mermaid/src` tree has Git object ID `f1a8a6774bd3a22d4983290fb812b43dd898b0dd` in both that commit and `rust-v0.162.1`. The TUI adapter is also identical, blob `446208fbb991bdc60716d4d8c77dd82d51640100`. There is no unreleased fix in these implementations at the inspected commit. - The merged [syntax expansion PR #48895](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/48895) covers directions, edge forms, and node groups. It does not add multiline node labels. This comparison checked source and Git object identities. I did not build or execute current `main`; a Rust toolchain was not installed. **Separate limits in the larger motivating diagram** My original diagram also contains longer labels: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Compatibility review
and resolver dry run passed"] --> B["Approve upgrade plan"] B --> C["Update OTel packages
and logging handler"] C --> D["Rebuild Docker stack
and verify collector records"] D --> E["Open PR"] ``` Flattening its breaks into spaces is not an adequate workaround. The first and fourth labels then occupy 48 and 49 ASCII display cells, respectively. They exceed the separate [`MAX_LABEL = 40` limit](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/cd8d61b223d95fd540bb646d627e7f0e7cfa6146/codex-rs/mermaid/src/lib.rs#L20-L24). Available terminal width is a third, later check. The short reproduction above isolates line-break support from both limits.
